claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for deployment, but only as a qualified certification with explicit disclosure of the small-business support slice weakness because aggregate performance passes while no approved mitigation removes the subgroup exposure.
specific_concerns: The admissible record available to this role is only the Actor's summary; the underlying contents of the cited evidence are not available for independent verification.
The Actor asserts a specific aggregate margin, specific subgroup shortfalls, and the absence of an approved mitigation, but those predicates are not directly inspectable here.

The policy threshold turns on whether the weakness is disclosed or an approved mitigation removes exposure; the packet describes what the certification record should say, but does not itself show the final disclosure record.
The Actor characterizes the subgroup as potentially material to a protected or contractual customer segment, but the materiality basis is not independently evidenced in the available record.
unsupported_claims: That the model passes the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
That the small-business support slice is exactly 1.1 percentage points below warning and 2.6 points below preferred threshold.
That no approved mitigation exists in the admissible record and only a draft monitoring proposal exists.
That a qualified certification record with the stated disclosure has actually been produced or approved.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying text or extracts for BMCARD-005-A through BMCARD-005-E showing the aggregate results, slice results, sampling note, mitigation status, and disclosure requirement.
Provide the final model-card certification/disclosure record to confirm the weakness is explicitly disclosed.
Provide the approval/status record for any mitigation proposal to verify whether deployment exposure has or has not been removed.

decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if the material weakness is actually disclosed, or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but cannot negate subgroup weakness.
Small-sample uncertainty may justify follow-up, but it does not convert an unresolved weakness into a clean certification.
Independent audit support requires the key factual predicates to be evidenced, not merely summarized by the Actor.
